feedback.problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i-4j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-4i+16j)\,\text{ft/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(8i-8j)\,\text{ft/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=2i-4j,\,u=-4i+16j,\,v=8i-8j
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 8i-8j & =(-4i+16j)+(2i-4j)t \\ 12i-24j & =(2i-4j)t \\ 12i-24j & =2ti-4tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}12 & = & 2t \\ -24 & = & -4t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,t=6\,\text{s}.
$$
